summary:
Have you ever wondered what it truly takes to design, launch, and command a deep space mission from the ground up?

Our project, Cyber Cosmos, is an interactive space mission architecture and simulation platform engineered to empower users to conceptualize, manage, and execute end to end aerospace missions from initial blueprint to orbital operation. 

By transcending conventional educational tools that examine disciplines like orbital mechanics or propulsion in isolation, Cyber Cosmos delivers a cohesive systems engineering environment. Participants navigate intricate multidisciplinary trade offs, calibrating scientific yield against payload mass, power budgets, telemetry volume, and capital expenditure while optimizing mission critical operational constraints. 

By bridging the divide between abstract academic theory and real world mission formulation, the platform cultivates rigorous systems thinking, enabling aspiring aerospace engineers to iterate, master complex constraints, and extract actionable insights from both mission triumphs and anomalies.

1. WHAT IS THIS?

FRONTIER MISSION IN SPACE is an interactive educational space mission design and simulation game developed on Roblox. It allows students to experience the process of planning, designing, building and launching their own space missions while learning about the engineering and scientific principles behind real-world space exploration.

Inspired by NASA's mission design resources, GMAT, Mission Design Lab and educational space games, AXEMU introduces students to the different stages of a space mission, from defining mission objectives to evaluating engineering requirements and simulating a rocket launch.

Players must make important decisions about rocket components, fuel, mass, electrical power, propulsion, communication systems and mission objectives. Every decision affects the mission's performance and chances of success. In addition, players can travel to the Moon, land on its surface and collect specific lunar rock samples to bring back to Earth for scientific research. Through this activity, students learn about lunar exploration, sample collection, scientific investigation and the importance of studying extraterrestrial materials to better understand the Moon and the history of our Solar System.

2.FEATURES :

Mission Planning System

  • Players select their mission objectives and determine the type of space mission they want to undertake.
  • They choose suitable orbits based on their mission requirements.
  • The system ensures that players plan their missions before building their rockets.

Rocket Workshop and 3D Component Preview

  • Players can build their own rockets by selecting different components.
  • Each component has a specific engineering function, helping players understand its importance.
  • A 3D preview allows players to examine and rotate rocket components from different angles.
  • Players learn how different components work together to form a complete spacecraft.

Engineering Calculation and Mission Verification

  • Players calculate important engineering data, including rocket mass, fuel capacity, thrust-to-weight ratio, electrical power and communication requirements.
  • The game evaluates whether the rocket meets the requirements of the selected mission.
  • Players receive feedback and recommendations when their rocket fails an engineering requirement.
  • Mission approval is required before launching, encouraging players to improve their designs.

Rocket Launch and Flight Simulation

  • Players can launch their completed rockets from a launch facility.
  • They can enter the cockpit and control the rocket during flight.
  • The simulation introduces the relationship between thrust, mass, gravity and rocket movement.
  • Players experience the excitement of launching a rocket after completing the necessary engineering tasks.

Lunar Landing and Rock Sample Collection

  • Players travel to the Moon and attempt to land their spacecraft on its surface.
  • They explore the lunar environment and collect specific rock samples for scientific research.
  • Players must complete their collection objectives and bring the samples back to Earth.
  • This feature introduces students to lunar exploration, geological research, sample collection and the importance of studying lunar materials to understand the Moon's formation and history.

Multiplayer Crew Experience

  • Up to four players can participate inside the rocket capsule, consisting of one pilot and three crew members.
  • Players can work together during the mission, share responsibilities and cooperate to achieve their objectives.
  • This encourages teamwork, communication and collaboration.

3. HOW DOES FRONTIER MISSION IN SPACE ACHIEVE THE OBJECTIVE?

Solving Mission Planning Challenges

  • Students choose scientific objectives and suitable orbits, learning how NASA plans missions around specific research goals and technical requirements.

Overcoming Rocket Engineering Challenges

  • Students design rockets and calculate mass, fuel, thrust and electrical power to overcome engineering constraints and build a mission-ready spacecraft.

Solving Technical Problems

  • Students identify failed engineering requirements, adjust their rocket designs and manage limited resources to improve mission performance.

Overcoming Lunar Exploration Challenges

  • Students simulate travelling to and landing on the Moon, collecting specific lunar rock samples and returning them to Earth for scientific research.

4. WHAT IMPACT WILL THIS GAME GIVE FOR BOTH STUDENTS AND THE EARTH?

Develop Future STEM Talent

  • Inspire students to pursue careers in aerospace engineering, astronomy, robotics and other STEM fields.

Improve Science and Engineering Education

  • Make complex scientific concepts easier to understand through practical simulations and interactive learning.

Strengthen Problem-Solving Skills

  • Train students to analyse challenges, manage limited resources and make decisions based on scientific data.

Encourage Innovation and Creativity

  • Allow students to experiment with different rocket designs and engineering solutions, developing creative thinking.

5. USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI)

ChatGPT

  • Used to generate and improve Roblox Lua scripts, develop game features and troubleshoot coding errors.
  • Helped organise project ideas and explain space engineering concepts.

DeepSeek

  • Used to assist with programming logic, review code and explore possible solutions to technical problems.

Claude AI

  • Used to refine game concepts, improve code structure and provide additional ideas for developing educational features.
